title: Mendix occupies the app-layer slot, so the only Mendix story is migrating one app to a typed spec
content:
This group is a negative finding recorded where a demo design would normally sit. Mendix occupies the app-layer slot, so there is no complementary integration to build — the research text rules the complement framing out explicitly. What remains is a migration story: one app rebuilt as a typed spec, shown as a substitution rather than an addition.

The targeting is as specific as the mechanism. The migration is aimed at deals too small to justify a seat, which moves the argument off capability and onto licence economics. That is a narrow wedge, and it is the only one this cohort supports.

The six leads are all Dutch and all deeply committed to the platform per their source rows — Benelux Partner of the Year, Mendix EXPERT, a dedicated low-code operating company, and combinations with SAP, Siemens PLM, OutSystems and Dynamics. Four are marked "2 · decide thesis first" and two "9 · do not pitch", so the corpus itself records that the displacement thesis is unresolved. The decision to be made is upstream of any pitch: whether Powerhouse competes for the app layer at all.
